::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Find $F(x)=\int_{x^2}^{e^x} \cos (t^3) \ dt $](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1141598/find-fx-int-x2ex-cos-t3-dt), asked by [Road Human](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/204093/road-human) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-02-10; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> If $$F(x)=\int_{x^2}^{e^x} \cos (t^3) \ dt$$
>
> Find $$\int F(x) dx$$
>
> I tried to find $$\int \cos (t^3) \ dt$$ but it is not success !
:::

There are two parts to the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.  One is that 
$$\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a)$$
where $F$ is an antiderivative of $f$.  The other part says that
$$\frac{d}{dx} \int_a^x f(t)\,dt = f(x)$$
This is the one that's relevant here.

Combining with the Chain Rule,
$$\frac{d}{dx} \int_a^{h(x)} f(t)\,dt = f(h(x))h'(x)$$
Finally,
$$\frac{d}{dx} \int_{g(x)}^{h(x)} f(t)\,dt = f(h(x))h'(x) - f(g(x))g'(x)$$
